notes: Textbook: no new NCERT Class XII Mathematics book exists for 2026-27; CBSE 2026-27 prescribes 'Mathematics Part I' and 'Part II' (NCERT) plus Exemplar and Lab Manual, editions unstated. I could not read the current Part I/Part II prelims (ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf is blocked by robots for my fetcher; an older 2019-20 Part I prelims was returned from cache), so the reprint year is not verified.

Section lists were DERIVED, not read from the current print: the pre-rationalisation contents (official, 2019-20) minus the sections NCERT's 2022 rationalisation list removes, cross-checked against the SATHEE reproduction. Section numbering in the current book may differ; titles only are recorded.

Conflicts between sources: SATHEE still shows '5.8 Mean Value Theorem' (Ch 5), a 'Properties of Determinants' heading (Ch 4), '8.2.1 area bounded by a curve and a line' (Ch 8), and the whole Plane material 11.6-11.10 (Ch 11), all of which the NCERT rationalisation list removes and none of which is in the CBSE 2026-27 topic list. I followed the rationalisation list and the CBSE curriculum and left them out.

Removed by rationalisation (not recorded): binary operations; elementary row/column operations and inverse by elementary operations; properties of determinants; Mean Value Theorem; tangents and normals; approximations; definite integral as a limit of a sum; area between two curves; formation of differential equations; scalar triple product; planes, coplanarity and line-plane angle; types of LPP section; random variables, probability distributions, mean/variance, Bernoulli trials and binomial distribution.

Chapter 1: CBSE 2026-27 lists only types of relations and one-one/onto functions; composition and invertible functions remain partly in the book (section 1.4) but are not in the CBSE topic list. Outcome o04 covers them as 'extension'. Chapter 2: only definitions, domain/range, principal value branch and graphs are listed by CBSE; the properties section was largely removed by rationalisation - the remaining 2.3 material was not checked, so only '2.1 Introduction' and '2.2 Basic Concepts' are recorded.

Existing competencies not used: MATH.coordinate.space-planes (planes are outside the 2026-27 syllabus) and MATH.probability.random-variables (random variables removed from the book and absent from CBSE 2026-27). MATH.algebra.inverse-functions is used only for the extension outcome in Chapter 1.

CBSE restrictions recorded in outcomes: non-commutativity examples restricted to order-2 square matrices; determinants up to 3x3; systems with unique solution only (2 or 3 variables); FTC without proof; areas under lines, circles, parabolas and ellipses in standard form only; linear DE of the forms dy/dx + py = q and dx/dy + p1 x = q1; LP with at most three non-trivial constraints; only derivatives of sin^-1 x, cos^-1 x, tan^-1 x among inverse trig derivatives.

Assessment (CBSE 2026-27): 80-mark 3-hour paper; 55% remembering/understanding, 25% applying, 20% analysing/evaluating/creating; no chapter-wise weightage; 33% internal choice. Internal assessment 20 = periodic tests 10 (three tests, best two averaged; suggested Jul-Aug, Nov, Dec-Jan) + mathematics activities 10 (10 Lab Manual activities with record 5, year-end activity test 3, viva-voce 2).

Chapter titles: Part I titles seen on official NCERT prelims (older printing; titles are unchanged by rationalisation) and Part II titles 'Integrals', 'Differential Equations', 'Linear Programming', 'Probability' match the CBSE curriculum. 'Application of Integrals', 'Vector Algebra' and 'Three Dimensional Geometry' are the printed titles as reported by secondary sources; CBSE names them 'Applications of the Integrals', 'Vectors' and 'Three-dimensional Geometry'; marked verified:false.
Several existing competencies are tagged 11-11 (e.g. MATH.algebra.relations, MATH.algebra.functions); they are used as prerequisites or partial fits here.

sections.title: Composition of Functions and Invertible Function

outcomes.statement: Test whether a given relation is reflexive, symmetric or transitive, and justify the answer.

proposed.name: Test relations for reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity and equivalence
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.relations (grade 11) is about representing relations; classifying them and finding equivalence classes is a distinct proof-oriented skill.

outcomes.statement: Show that a relation is an equivalence relation and describe its equivalence classes.

proposed.name: Test relations for reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity and equivalence
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.relations (grade 11) is about representing relations; classifying them and finding equivalence classes is a distinct proof-oriented skill.

outcomes.statement: Decide whether a function is one-one, onto or bijective, using algebraic arguments or graphs.

proposed.name: Classify functions as one-one, onto or bijective
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.inverse-functions uses bijectivity but deciding injectivity/surjectivity of a given function is a separate, separately assessed skill.

outcomes.statement: (Extension; in book, not in CBSE 2026-27 topic list) Compose functions and find the inverse of a bijective function.

proposed.name: Combine functions by sum, difference, product, quotient and composition
proposed.why: No existing competency covers the algebra of functions or composition; MATH.algebra.inverse-functions presupposes it.

outcomes.statement: Explain why trigonometric functions must be restricted to be invertible and state domain, range and principal value branch of each inverse function.

proposed.name: Classify functions as one-one, onto or bijective
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.inverse-functions uses bijectivity but deciding injectivity/surjectivity of a given function is a separate, separately assessed skill.

outcomes.statement: Find principal values of inverse trigonometric expressions.
Sketch the graphs of inverse trigonometric functions by reflecting the restricted trigonometric graphs in y = x.
Evaluate compositions such as sin(sin^-1 x) or sin^-1(sin x) correctly using the principal branch.
Read and construct matrices from data or a rule, state their order, identify types (row, column, square, diagonal, scalar, identity, zero) and use equality of matrices.
Add matrices, multiply by a scalar and multiply conformable matrices.
Use properties of matrix operations and show with order-2 examples that multiplication is not commutative and that AB = O is possible with A, B non-zero.
Find transposes, use (AB)' = B'A', and write a square matrix as a sum of symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices.

proposed.name: Use transposes and symmetric/skew-symmetric decomposition
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.matrices covers matrix operations; transpose laws and writing a square matrix as symmetric plus skew-symmetric parts form a distinct skill.

outcomes.statement: Explain invertibility of a square matrix and prove that an inverse, if it exists, is unique.
Model simple real situations (costs, quantities) with matrix products.

sections.title: Adjoint and Inverse of a Matrix

outcomes.statement: Evaluate determinants of square matrices up to order 3.
concepts: expansion along a row or column

outcomes.statement: Use determinants to find the area of a triangle from vertex coordinates and to test collinearity or find an unknown vertex.
Find minors, cofactors and the adjoint of a matrix and use A(adj A) = |A| I.

proposed.name: Find minors, cofactors, adjoint and inverse of a square matrix (up to 3x3)
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.determinants is evaluation and simple uses; the cofactor/adjoint route to A^-1 is a multi-step skill that matrix-systems depends on.

outcomes.statement: Decide whether a matrix is singular and find the inverse of a non-singular matrix of order up to 3.

proposed.name: Find minors, cofactors, adjoint and inverse of a square matrix (up to 3x3)
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.determinants is evaluation and simple uses; the cofactor/adjoint route to A^-1 is a multi-step skill that matrix-systems depends on.

outcomes.statement: Decide from examples whether a system of linear equations is consistent and how many solutions it has.
Solve systems of two or three linear equations with a unique solution using X = A^-1 B, including word problems.

proposed.name: Find minors, cofactors, adjoint and inverse of a square matrix (up to 3x3)
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.determinants is evaluation and simple uses; the cofactor/adjoint route to A^-1 is a multi-step skill that matrix-systems depends on.

sections.title: Derivatives of Functions in Parametric Forms

outcomes.statement: Test continuity of a function at a point and on its domain, including piecewise functions, and find parameter values that make a function continuous.
Test differentiability at a point and explain that differentiability implies continuity but not conversely.
Differentiate composite functions by the chain rule, including sin^-1 x, cos^-1 x and tan^-1 x.
Differentiate exponential and logarithmic functions and their combinations.
Differentiate implicitly defined functions, functions in parametric form, and functions of the form u(x)^v(x) by logarithmic differentiation.

proposed.name: Differentiate implicit, parametric and logarithmically transformed functions
proposed.why: MATH.calculus.derivative-rules covers sum/product/quotient/chain rules; implicit, parametric and logarithmic differentiation are separate techniques.

outcomes.statement: Find second-order derivatives and verify given differential relations.

proposed.name: Find and use second-order derivatives
proposed.why: No existing competency covers second derivatives (including verifying relations such as y'' + y = 0), which the second-derivative test also needs.

outcomes.statement: Use derivatives to find rates of change of related quantities (areas, volumes, marginal cost/revenue).
Find intervals on which a function is increasing or decreasing using the sign of its derivative.

proposed.name: Find intervals where a function increases or decreases
proposed.why: MATH.calculus.applications is about rates and extrema; sign analysis of f' to find monotonic intervals is a separate, frequently assessed skill.

outcomes.statement: Locate local maxima and minima using the first-derivative test.
Use the second-derivative test to classify critical points.

proposed.name: Find and use second-order derivatives
proposed.why: No existing competency covers second derivatives (including verifying relations such as y'' + y = 0), which the second-derivative test also needs.

outcomes.statement: Find absolute maximum and minimum values of a function on a closed interval.
Formulate and solve optimisation problems from geometry and everyday contexts.

sections.title: Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation
Evaluation of Definite Integrals by Substitution

outcomes.statement: Find antiderivatives of standard functions using integration as the inverse of differentiation and basic properties of indefinite integrals.
Integrate by substitution, including use of trigonometric identities.
Evaluate integrals of the specified standard forms such as 1/(x^2 +/- a^2), 1/sqrt(a^2 - x^2), (px+q)/(ax^2+bx+c) and sqrt(x^2 +/- a^2).
Integrate rational functions by decomposing them into partial fractions.

proposed.name: Integrate rational functions by partial fractions
proposed.why: MATH.calculus.integration-methods (and its MLY parts) names substitution and parts only; partial-fraction decomposition is a separate method.

outcomes.statement: Integrate by parts, including integrals of the form e^x[f(x) + f'(x)].
Evaluate definite integrals using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (stated without proof), including by substitution.
Use properties of definite integrals (e.g. f(a+b-x), odd/even functions, splitting the interval) to evaluate integrals.

proposed.name: Evaluate definite integrals using their properties
proposed.why: Using symmetry/King's-rule style properties (e.g. integral of f(a+b-x), odd/even functions) is a distinct skill beyond evaluation via antiderivatives.

outcomes.statement: Express the area between a curve and an axis as a definite integral using vertical or horizontal strips.
Find areas bounded by lines and the coordinate axes using integration.
Find areas of regions bounded by circles, parabolas and ellipses in standard form.
Sketch the region before integrating and choose limits correctly, using symmetry where possible.

sections.title: General and Particular Solutions of a Differential Equation
Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

outcomes.statement: Find the order and degree (when defined) of a differential equation.
Verify that a function is a general or particular solution of a given differential equation.

proposed.name: Find and use second-order derivatives
proposed.why: No existing competency covers second derivatives (including verifying relations such as y'' + y = 0), which the second-derivative test also needs.

outcomes.statement: Solve differential equations by separation of variables, including initial-value problems.
Recognise and solve homogeneous first-order first-degree differential equations with the substitution y = vx.

proposed.name: Solve homogeneous first-order first-degree differential equations
proposed.why: MATH.calculus.differential-equations is elementary solving (separation); the y = vx substitution method is a separate technique.

outcomes.statement: Solve linear differential equations dy/dx + Py = Q or dx/dy + P1 x = Q1 using an integrating factor.

proposed.name: Solve linear first-order differential equations with an integrating factor

outcomes.statement: Model simple growth, decay or geometric situations with a first-order differential equation and solve it.

sections.title: Multiplication of a Vector by a Scalar

outcomes.statement: Distinguish scalars from vectors, find magnitude and identify zero, unit, equal, negative, collinear and co-initial vectors.

Find the position vector of a point dividing a segment internally or externally in a given ratio.

sections.title: Direction Cosines and Direction Ratios of a Line
Equation of a Line in Space

outcomes.statement: Find direction cosines and direction ratios of a line, including the line through two points.

proposed.name: Find direction cosines and direction ratios of vectors and lines
proposed.why: Shared by Vector Algebra and Three Dimensional Geometry; neither MATH.vectors.algebra nor MATH.coordinate.space-lines names it.

sections.title: Linear Programming Problem and its Mathematical Formulation
